claim: Rb contains 16 putative Cdk phosphorylation sites spread throughout the protein.
source: Rb contains 16 putative Cdk phosphorylation sites that are spread throughout the protein, and all but one (S567) lie outside of Rb's structured A'/B' and A/B-box or 'pocket' protein–protein binding domains (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number and distribution of Cdk phosphorylation sites on Rb, referencing Figure 1A for visual support.

claim: All but one Cdk phosphorylation site (S567) lie outside of Rb's structured pocket domains.
source: Rb contains 16 putative Cdk phosphorylation sites that are spread throughout the protein, and all but one (S567) lie outside of Rb's structured A'/B' and A/B-box or 'pocket' protein–protein binding domains (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the location of Cdk sites relative to Rb's structured domains.

claim: Rb is thought to exist in three generalized isoforms: un-phosphorylated, hypo-phosphorylated, and inactive hyper-phosphorylated.
source: Rb is thought to exist in three generalized isoforms: (1) un-phosphorylated Rb; (2) hypo-phosphorylated Rb, also referred to as 'under' phosphorylated Rb or 'partially' phosphorylated Rb; and (3) inactive hyper-phosphorylated Rb, present in late G1, S, G2 and M phases that is readily identifiable by SDS-PAGE as a slower migrating species (Burkhart and Sage, 2008; Paternot et al., 2010; Henley and Dick, 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple references supporting this established model of Rb isoforms.

claim: The biologically active isoform(s) of Rb required for early G1 phase regulation, DNA damage checkpoint control, cell cycle exit, and differentiation remains unknown.
source: Surprisingly, given the scientific scrutiny of Rb over the last 25 years, the biochemical identification of the biologically active isoform(s) of Rb required for early G1 phase regulation, DNA damage checkpoint control, cell cycle exit, and differentiation remains unknown.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this knowledge gap as motivation for the study.

claim: Supra-physiologic overexpression of cyclins and Cdks results in Rb inactivation by hyper-phosphorylation associated with accelerated S-phase entry.
source: To dissect Rb function and regulation, many early reports utilized supra-physiologic overexpression studies using various cyclins (A, B, D, E) and Cdks (−1, −2, −4, −6) that resulted in Rb inactivation by hyper-phosphorylation associated with an accelerated S-phase entry, and induction of E2F-dependent target genes (Hinds et al., 1992; Ewen et al., 1993; Resnitzky et al., 1994; Lundberg and Weinberg, 1998).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies demonstrating this effect.

claim: The widely accepted model proposes that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 inactivates Rb during early G1 phase by progressive multi-phosphorylation termed 'hypo-phosphorylation'.
source: Collectively, over the last 20 years, these studies have led to a widely accepted model of G1 cell cycle progression that proposes cyclin D:Cdk4/6 inactivates Rb during early G1 phase by progressive multi-phosphorylation, termed 'hypo-phosphorylation', resulting in release of E2F transcription factors that induce expression of cyclin E, resulting in activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes that complete Rb inactivation by hyper-phosphorylation in late G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript describes the prevailing model in the field.

claim: Putative hypo-phosphorylated Rb and un-phosphorylated Rb co-migrate on 1D SDS-PAGE and cannot be separated.
source: The key tenet of this model is the progressive multi-phosphorylating, hypo-phosphorylation of Rb by cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes; however, the putative hypo-phosphorylated Rb and un-phosphorylated Rb co-migrate on 1D SDS-PAGE and cannot be separated (Ezhevsky et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites a reference demonstrating this technical limitation.

claim: There is no biochemical data defining the extent or timing of phosphorylation that constitutes hypo-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Moreover, there is no biochemical data defining the extent or timing of phosphorylation that constitutes hypo-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this knowledge gap.

claim: The core tenet that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 inactivates Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylation remains unproven biochemically.
source: Thus, the critical core tenet of the G1 model that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 inactivates Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylation or hypo-phosphorylation remains unproven biochemically.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly challenges the prevailing model based on lack of biochemical evidence.

claim: Cyclin D:Cdk4/6 is constitutively active throughout early G1 phase at the same time when Rb is repressing E2F target genes.
source: We have previously found in kinetic analyses from highly synchronized normal cells and p16-deficient cancer cells that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 is constitutively active throughout early G1 phase at the same time when Rb is repressing E2F target genes (Ezhevsky et al., 1997, 2001; Haberichter et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies by the authors demonstrating this observation.

claim: Induction of E2F target genes is observed only upon activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes and appearance of hyper-phosphorylated Rb.
source: In fact, we only observed induction of E2F target genes upon the activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes and the appearance of hyper-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript describes observations from previous studies.

claim: Rb is exclusively mono-phosphorylated in early G1 phase in both normal and p16-deficient tumor cells.
source: Here, for the first time, we separated all Rb isoforms by two-dimensional isoelectric focusing (2D IEF) and find that Rb is exclusively mono-phosphorylated in early G1 phase in both normal and p16-deficient tumor cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a key finding from 2D IEF experiments.

claim: Cyclin D:Cdk4/6 is the Rb mono-phosphorylating kinase that generates 14 independent mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms in early G1 phase.
source: Using Cdk4/6-specific inhibitors and triple cyclin D-deleted MEFs, we determined that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 is the Rb mono-phosphorylating kinase that generates 14 independent mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms in early G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript describes experiments using inhibitors and genetic deletion to identify the kinase.

claim: At the late G1 Restriction Point, cyclin E:Cdk2 inactivates Rb by quantum hyper-phosphorylation.
source: At the late G1 Restriction Point, activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes perform a quantum hyper-phosphorylating inactivation of all mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a key finding from the study.

claim: Cells undergoing a DNA damage response activate cyclin D:Cdk4/6 to generate mono-phosphorylated Rb that regulates global transcription.
source: Cells undergoing a DNA damage response activate cyclin D:Cdk4/6 to generate mono-phosphorylated Rb that regulates global transcription, whereas cells undergoing differentiation utilize un-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a key finding from DNA damage experiments.

claim: Cells undergoing differentiation utilize un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Cells undergoing a DNA damage response activate cyclin D:Cdk4/6 to generate mono-phosphorylated Rb that regulates global transcription, whereas cells undergoing differentiation utilize un-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a key finding from differentiation experiments.

claim: Mono-phosphorylated Rb is the only Rb isoform in early G1 phase.
source: These observations fundamentally change our understanding of G1 cell cycle progression and show that mono-phosphorylated Rb, generated by cyclin D:Cdk4/6, is the only Rb isoform in early G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a major conclusion from the study.

claim: The Rb gene is infrequently mutated or deleted in human cancers.
source: However, the Rb gene is infrequently mutated or deleted, instead upstream pathways that regulate Rb by phosphorylation on Cdk sites are altered in the majority of human cancers, including deletion and mutation of the p16 tumor suppressor and upregulation and mutation of cyclin D1, D2, D3, Cdk4 and Cdk6 genes (Sherr and McCormick, 2002; Knudsen and Knudsen, 2006; Burkhart and Sage, 2008; Henley and Dick, 2012; Choi and Anders, 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple references supporting this statement about cancer genetics.

claim: Upstream pathways that regulate Rb by phosphorylation on Cdk sites are altered in the majority of human cancers.
source: However, the Rb gene is infrequently mutated or deleted, instead upstream pathways that regulate Rb by phosphorylation on Cdk sites are altered in the majority of human cancers, including deletion and mutation of the p16 tumor suppressor and upregulation and mutation of cyclin D1, D2, D3, Cdk4 and Cdk6 genes (Sherr and McCormick, 2002; Knudsen and Knudsen, 2006; Burkhart and Sage, 2008; Henley and Dick, 2012; Choi and Anders, 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple references supporting this statement about cancer genetics.

claim: Rb contains 15 putative Cdk phosphorylation sites located on loops between or after structured A'/B' and A/B pocket domains.
source: Rb contains 15 putative Cdk phosphorylation sites located on loops between or after structured A'/B' and A/B pocket domains (Burke et al., 2012; Lamber et al., 2013) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript cites structural studies and references Figure 1A showing the location of these sites.

claim: Primary human foreskin fibroblasts arrested in early G1 phase by contact inhibition progress through early G1 phase with constitutively active cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes.
source: Analysis of synchronized primary human foreskin fibroblasts (HFFs) arrested in early G1 phase by contact inhibition in the presence of serum and released by replating at low density progressed through early G1 phase with constitutively active cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes and no evidence for increased Rb phosphorylation or transcriptional induction of Cdc6, a key E2F target gene repressed by active Rb (Morris and Dyson, 2001) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Cdc6 is a key E2F target gene repressed by active Rb.
source: Analysis of synchronized primary human foreskin fibroblasts (HFFs) arrested in early G1 phase by contact inhibition in the presence of serum and released by replating at low density progressed through early G1 phase with constitutively active cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes and no evidence for increased Rb phosphorylation or transcriptional induction of Cdc6, a key E2F target gene repressed by active Rb (Morris and Dyson, 2001) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript cites a reference supporting this statement about Cdc6.

claim: Cdc6 was induced ten-fold upon cyclin E:Cdk2 activation and Rb hyper-phosphorylation.
source: In contrast, Cdc6 was induced ten-fold upon cyclin E:Cdk2 activation and Rb hyper-phosphorylation, which migrates more slowly on 1D SDS-PAGE.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from kinetic analysis.

claim: Hyper-phosphorylated Rb migrates more slowly on 1D SDS-PAGE.
source: In contrast, Cdc6 was induced ten-fold upon cyclin E:Cdk2 activation and Rb hyper-phosphorylation, which migrates more slowly on 1D SDS-PAGE.
evidence: The manuscript describes the migration pattern of hyper-phosphorylated Rb.

claim: Putative hypo-phosphorylated Rb isoforms co-migrated as a single fastest migrating species during all early G1 phase time points.
source: However, the putative hypo-phosphorylated Rb isoforms co-migrated as a single fastest migrating species during all of the early G1 phase time points (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental observations from Figure 1B.

claim: 1D SDS-PAGE is not capable of separating all Rb phospho-isoforms.
source: Thus, there is either no evidence for progressive hypo-phosphorylation of Rb and/or 1D SDS-PAGE is not capable of separating all Rb phospho-isoforms.
evidence: The manuscript infers this limitation from the inability to detect progressive phosphorylation by 1D SDS-PAGE.

claim: Phosphates are highly acidic modifications that significantly change the isoelectric point (pI) of a protein.
source: Phosphates are highly acidic modifications that significantly change the isoelectric point (pI) of a protein.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Two-dimensional isoelectric focusing (2D IEF) can separate specific phospho-isoforms of a protein based on total phosphate numbers regardless of position within the protein or nature of the modified residue.
source: Unlike 1D SDS-PAGE, two-dimensional isoelectric focusing (2D IEF) can separate specific phospho-isoforms of a protein based on total phosphate numbers regardless of position within the protein or nature of the modified residue (Figure 1C).
evidence: The manuscript describes the principle of 2D IEF and references Figure 1C.

claim: The isoelectric point of un-phosphorylated Rb is 8.1.
source: The isoelectric point of un-phosphorylated Rb is 8.1, and 2D IEF of the ΔCdk Rb construct expressed in asynchronous cycling cells focused as a single basic species with a pI ∼8 (Figure 1D), confirming that Rb is only phosphorylated on Cdk sites and that S567 is not phosphorylated in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript states the theoretical pI and confirms it experimentally in Figure 1D.

claim: Rb is only phosphorylated on Cdk sites in vivo.
source: The isoelectric point of un-phosphorylated Rb is 8.1, and 2D IEF of the ΔCdk Rb construct expressed in asynchronous cycling cells focused as a single basic species with a pI ∼8 (Figure 1D), confirming that Rb is only phosphorylated on Cdk sites and that S567 is not phosphorylated in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript confirms this by showing that the ΔCdk construct is not phosphorylated.

claim: S567 is not phosphorylated in vivo.
source: The isoelectric point of un-phosphorylated Rb is 8.1, and 2D IEF of the ΔCdk Rb construct expressed in asynchronous cycling cells focused as a single basic species with a pI ∼8 (Figure 1D), confirming that Rb is only phosphorylated on Cdk sites and that S567 is not phosphorylated in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript confirms this by showing that the ΔCdk construct (which retains S567) is not phosphorylated.

claim: S567 is buried in the central core of Rb's A-box and solvent inaccessible.
source: We left S567 unaltered because it is buried in the central core of Rb's A-box and solvent inaccessible (Lee et al., 1998).
evidence: The manuscript cites a structural study supporting this statement.

claim: Single Cdk site Rb construct (Rb1xCdk) expressed in cycling cells focused as a single phosphorylated Rb species with a more acidic pI ∼7.0.
source: 2D IEF of single Cdk site Rb1xCdk construct expressed in cycling cells focused as a single phosphorylated Rb species with a more acidic pI ∼7.0, that we termed mono-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 1D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The double Cdk site Rb2xCdk construct focused as two spots: mono-phosphorylated Rb and di-phosphorylated Rb.
source: The double Cdk site Rb2xCdk construct focused as two spots: mono-phosphorylated Rb and di-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from 2D IEF.

claim: 2D IEF of the Rb3xCdk construct focused as mono-phosphorylated and tri-phosphorylated Rb, with no di-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Surprisingly, 2D IEF of the Rb3xCdk construct focused as mono-phosphorylated and tri-phosphorylated Rb, with no di-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 1D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 2D IEF of Rb constructs containing six, nine, and fifteen Cdk sites resulted in the appearance of mono-phosphorylated Rb plus either a six, nine, or >12 phosphate Rb species, with absence of intermediate Rb phospho-isoforms.
source: Likewise, 2D IEF of Rb constructs containing six (Rb6xCdk), nine (Rb9xCdk) and fifteen (Rb15xCdk) Cdk sites resulted in the appearance of mono-phosphorylated Rb, plus either a six, nine, or >12 phosphate (pI < 4) Rb species, respectively, and the absence of any intermediate Rb phospho-isoforms (Figure 1D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 2D IEF quantitatively separated all Rb isoforms from un-phosphorylated Rb to mono-phosphorylated Rb and all multi-phosphorylated Rb isoforms up to hyper-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Thus, unlike 1D SDS-PAGE, 2D IEF quantitatively separated all Rb isoforms from un-phosphorylated Rb to mono-phosphorylated Rb and all multi-phosphorylated Rb isoforms up to hyper-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the capability of 2D IEF based on the experimental results.

claim: Rb from serum deprived G0 arrested primary HFFs focused as a single, basic isoform with a pI ∼8.
source: Consistent with no 32P-labeling of Rb from G0 arrested cells (DeCaprio et al., 1989; Ezhevsky et al., 2001), Rb from serum deprived G0 arrested primary HFFs focused as a single, basic isoform with a pI ∼8 (Figure 1E).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1E and cites previous studies.

claim: Rb from contact inhibited early G1 phase arrested HFFs focused as a single mono-phosphorylated species with a pI ∼7.0.
source: In contrast, Rb from contact inhibited early G1 phase arrested (+FBS) HFFs focused as a single mono-phosphorylated species with a pI ∼7.0 (Figure 1E).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Lambda phosphatase treatment of contact inhibited mono-phosphorylated Rb collapsed into un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Lambda phosphatase treatment of contact inhibited mono-phosphorylated Rb collapsed into un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 1E).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Rb from asynchronously cycling primary HFFs focused as two isoforms: mono-phosphorylated Rb plus a very acidic hyper-phosphorylated Rb isoform (pI < 4).
source: 2D IEF of Rb from asynchronously cycling primary HFFs focused as two isoforms: mono-phosphorylated Rb plus a very acidic hyper-phosphorylated Rb isoform (pI < 4) (Figure 1E).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The majority of human tumors expressing wild-type Rb contain oncogenic mutations that upregulate cyclin D:Cdk4/6 kinase activity.
source: The majority of human tumors expressing wild-type Rb contain oncogenic mutations that upregulate cyclin D:Cdk4/6 kinase activity (Sherr and McCormick, 2002; Choi and Anders, 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites references supporting this statement about cancer genetics.

claim: 2D IEF of Rb from cycling HCT116, H1299, U2OS, and HL60 tumor cell lines showed the presence of only mono-phosphorylated Rb and hyper-phosphorylated Rb, with no evidence of multi-phosphorylated, hypo-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
source: Surprisingly, 2D IEF of Rb from cycling populations of all four tumor cell lines, HCT116 colon carcinoma, H1299 lung adenocarcinoma, U2OS osteosarcoma, and HL60 promyelocytic leukemia, showed the presence of only mono-phosphorylated Rb and hyper-phosphorylated Rb, with no evidence of multi-phosphorylated, hypo-phosphorylated Rb isoforms, even though cyclin D:Cdk4/6 was deregulated in all four tumor cell types (Figure 1F).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1F.

claim: G0-arrested cells contain un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Together, these results present several significant insights into the biochemical properties of Rb phosphorylation in vivo. First, G0-arrested cells contain un-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from 2D IEF experiments.

claim: Rb from both cycling normal and p16-deleted tumor cells is only mono-phosphorylated or hyper-phosphorylated in vivo.
source: Second, Rb from both cycling normal and p16-deleted tumor cells is only mono-phosphorylated or hyper-phosphorylated in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from 2D IEF experiments.

claim: Rb phosphorylation is performed by two entirely independent cyclin:Cdk activities: a Rb mono-phosphorylating Cdk activity and a Rb hyper-phosphorylating Cdk activity.
source: Third, these observations point to phosphorylation of Rb by two entirely independent cyclin:Cdk activities: (1) a Rb mono-phosphorylating Cdk activity that places one, and only one, phosphate on Rb; and (2) a Rb hyper-phosphorylating Cdk activity that places >12 phosphates on Rb.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the observation of only mono- and hyper-phosphorylated forms.

claim: G0 cells contained only un-phosphorylated Rb, but by 1 hr post-stimulation, a small amount of mono-phosphorylated was detected, concurrent with activation of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes.
source: G0 cells contained only un-phosphorylated Rb, but by 1 hr post-stimulation, a small amount of mono-phosphorylated was detected, concurrent with activation of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Rb remained exclusively mono-phosphorylated throughout the entire early G1 phase time points at 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14 hr with no higher order phosphorylation species detected.
source: Surprisingly, Rb remained exclusively mono-phosphorylated throughout the entire early G1 phase time points at 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12. and 14 hr with no higher order phosphorylation species detected (Figure 1G), even though cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes were constitutively active.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1G.

claim: At 16 hr post-release, a quantum switch-like shift to hyper-phosphorylated Rb was detected concomitant with activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes.
source: At 16 hr post-release, we detected a quantum switch-like shift to hyper-phosphorylated Rb concomitant with activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Rb remained exclusively mono-phosphorylated throughout the entire early G1 phase time points from 0 to 7 hr in contact inhibited and released HFFs with no higher order Rb phosphorylation species detected.
source: Rb remained exclusively mono-phosphorylated throughout the entire early G1 phase time points from 0 to 7 hr with no higher order Rb phosphorylation species detected (Figure 1H).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1H.

claim: At 10 hr post-release, a strong shift to hyper-phosphorylated Rb (>12 phosphates) was detected, concomitant with activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes and transcriptional induction of cdc6.
source: At 10 hr post-release, we detected a strong shift to hyper-phosphorylated Rb (>12 phosphates), concomitant with activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes and transcriptional induction of cdc6, an E2F target gene (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Contact inhibited early G1-arrested U2OS cells contained only mono-phosphorylated Rb, with no higher order Rb phosphorylated species, and active cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes.
source: Contact inhibited early G1-arrested U2OS cells (+FBS) contained only mono-phosphorylated Rb, with no higher order Rb phosphorylated species, and active cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rb remained exclusively mono-phosphorylated throughout all of the early G1 phase time points at 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 hr in U2OS cells in the presence of constitutively active cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes with no evidence of progressive hypo-phosphorylation.
source: Rb remained exclusively mono-phosphorylated throughout all of the early G1 phase time points at 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 hr in the presence of constitutively active cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes with no evidence of progressive hypo-phosphorylation.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from kinetic analysis.

claim: Both primary and tumor cells exclusively generate mono-phosphorylated Rb during all of early G1 phase before being converted in a quantum step to hyper-phosphorylated Rb at the late G1 phase Restriction Point.
source: Together, these observations demonstrated that both primary and tumor cells exclusively generate mono-phosphorylated Rb during all of early G1 phase before being converted in a quantum step to hyper-phosphorylated Rb at the late G1 phase Restriction Point.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from kinetic analyses.

claim: Hundreds of 2D IEFs on Rb from 11 cell types found no biochemical evidence to support the notion of progressive multi-phosphorylation or hypo-phosphorylation of Rb in early G1 phase.
source: Collectively, we performed hundreds of 2D IEFs on Rb from 11 cell types and found no biochemical evidence to support the notion of progressive multi-phosphorylation or hypo-phosphorylation of Rb in early G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the extensive experimental work performed.

claim: Mittnacht et al. (1994) reported that tryptic phospho-peptide mapping of total Rb isolated from early G1 phase cells retained the vast majority of the same phospho-peptide spots that hyper-phosphorylated Rb contained.
source: However, Mittnacht et al. (1994) reported that tryptic phospho-peptide mapping (where the 32P-labeled protein is cleaved into small peptides by trypsin digestion and then separated by charge and hydrophobicity) of total Rb isolated from early G1 phase cells (labeled as hypo-phosphorylated Rb) retained the vast majority of the same phospho-peptide spots that hyper-phosphorylated Rb contained.
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study's findings.

claim: The Mittnacht et al. (1994) study suggested the potential for the presence of many mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
source: In light of our new observations showing only mono-phosphorylated Rb present in early G1 phase, the Mittnacht et al. (1994) study suggested the potential for the presence of many mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms that when summed together would result in the observed phospho-peptide pattern.
evidence: The manuscript infers this interpretation from the Mittnacht et al. study in light of their new findings.

claim: All phospho-specific Rb antibodies recognized mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms from early G1 phase arrested cells, including S249/S252, T373, S608, S612, S795, S807/S811, T821 and T826.
source: While none of the antibodies recognized un-phosphorylated Rb from G0 arrested HFFs, all of the phospho-specific Rb antibodies recognized mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms from early G1 phase arrested cells, including S249/S252, T373, S608, S612, S795, S807/S811, T821 and T826 (Figure 2A).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: All of the phospho-specific antibodies recognized hyper-phosphorylated Rb from S phase arrested cells.
source: We also note that all of the phospho-specific antibodies recognized hyper-phosphorylated Rb from S phase arrested cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There are at least 8 individual mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
source: Together, these observations suggested the presence of at least 8 individual mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the phospho-specific antibody results.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of T826 mono-phosphorylated Rb was only recognized by immunoblot with the T826 phospho-specific antibody and not by T373, S608, S612, or S795 phospho-specific antibodies.
source: Consistent with the 2D IEF data, the phospho-specific immunoprecipitation of T826 mono-phosphorylated Rb was only recognized by immunoblot with the T826 phospho-specific antibody and not by T373, S608, S612, or S795 phospho-specific antibodies.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from phospho-specific immunoprecipitation.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of S608 mono-phosphorylated Rb was only recognized by the S608 phospho-specific antibody and not by the other phospho-specific antibodies.
source: Likewise, immunoprecipitation of S608 mono-phosphorylated Rb was only recognized by the S608 phospho-specific antibody and not by the other phospho-specific antibodies.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from phospho-specific immunoprecipitation.

claim: Immunoprecipitated hyper-phosphorylated Rb from S phase arrested HFF cells with either the T826 or S608 phospho-specific antibodies was recognized by multiple phospho-specific antibodies.
source: In contrast, immunoprecipitated hyper-phosphorylated Rb from S phase arrested HFF cells with either the T826 or S608 phospho-specific antibodies was recognized by multiple phospho-specific antibodies (Figure 2B), supporting the presence of multiple phosphates on individual hyper-phosphorylated Rb molecules.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 14 of the single Cdk site Rb constructs were mono-phosphorylated in vivo.
source: 2D IEFs on each of the single Cdk site Rb constructs expressed in cells determined that 14 of the single Cdk site Rb constructs were mono-phosphorylated in vivo (Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: T5 is not evolutionary conserved below primates and was not phosphorylated.
source: T5, which is not evolutionary conserved below primates, was not phosphorylated.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from 2D IEF of single Cdk site constructs.

claim: There are 14 independent mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms in early G1 phase.
source: Together, these observations demonstrate the presence of 14 independent mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms in early G1 phase and explain the large number of Rb tryptic phospho-peptide spots observed by Mittnacht et al. (1994).
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from single Cdk site construct experiments.

claim: Some, most or all of the 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms must be biologically active.
source: Moreover, because early G1 phase cells exclusively contain mono-phosphorylated Rb, by definition, some, most or all of the 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms must be biologically active.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the exclusive presence of mono-phosphorylated Rb in early G1 phase.

claim: Rb has been shown to bind to four members of the E2F family of transcription factors (E2F1-4) and over 100 additional cellular proteins.
source: Rb has been shown to bind to four members of the E2F family of transcription factors (E2F1-4) and over 100 additional cellular proteins (Morris and Dyson, 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites a reference supporting this statement about Rb binding partners.

claim: The generation of 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms may serve as a post-translational mechanism to diversify Rb into 14 independently functionalized mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms that each bind specific cellular targets during early G1 phase.
source: We hypothesized that the generation of 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms may serve as a post-translational mechanism to diversify Rb from a single un-phosphorylated protein in G0 into 14 independently functionalized mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms that each bind specific cellular targets during early G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a hypothesis to be tested.

claim: The E1a oncoprotein bound equally well to un-phosphorylated Rb and all 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
source: Given it's role in driving adenovirus infected quiescent G0 cells (containing un-phosphorylated Rb) into G1 phase and then S phase, it was not too surprising that the E1a oncoprotein bound equally well to un-phosphorylated Rb and all 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: None of the mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms were completely inactive for binding to E2Fs.
source: Surprisingly, we found that none of the mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms were completely inactive for binding to E2Fs and that each E2F showed a preferential binding specificity for individual mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Each E2F showed a preferential binding specificity for individual mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
source: Surprisingly, we found that none of the mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms were completely inactive for binding to E2Fs and that each E2F showed a preferential binding specificity for individual mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: E2F1 showed enhanced binding to Rb when it was mono-phosphorylated at positions S230, S249, T356 and S612.
source: E2F1 showed enhanced binding to Rb when it was mono-phosphorylated at positions S230, S249, T356 and S612 and decreased avidity when Rb was mono-phosphorylated at positions S608, S795 and T826 (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: E2F1 showed decreased avidity when Rb was mono-phosphorylated at positions S608, S795 and T826.
source: E2F1 showed enhanced binding to Rb when it was mono-phosphorylated at positions S230, S249, T356 and S612 and decreased avidity when Rb was mono-phosphorylated at positions S608, S795 and T826 (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: E2F4 showed decreased binding when Rb was mono-phosphorylated at positions S249, T373, S780 and T826.

evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Contact inhibited TKO cyclin D− MEFs contained only un-phosphorylated Rb.

evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Retroviral expression of cyclin D1 in contact inhibited TKO cyclin D− MEFs resulted in the appearance of mono-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Retroviral expression of cyclin D1 in contact inhibited TKO cyclin D− MEFs resulted in the appearance of mono-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Treatment of HFFs with the Cdk4/6 inhibitor at restimulation resulted in the presence of un-phosphorylated Rb, whereas control DMSO-treated cells contained mono-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Consistent with TKO cyclin D− MEFS, treatment of HFFs with the Cdk4/6 inhibitor at restimulation (+FBS) resulted in the presence of un-phosphorylated Rb, whereas control DMSO-treated cells contained mono-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 3C).

claim: Specific inhibition of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes by retroviral expression of p16 resulted in the presence of un-phosphorylated Rb.

evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Three independent approaches (genetic TKO cyclin D− MEFs, expression of p16, treatment with Cdk4/6 inhibitor) in three different cell types (MEFs, HFFs, U2OS) confirmed that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 was the Rb mono-phosphorylating kinase in vivo.
source: Collectively, these results from three independent approaches (genetic TKO cyclin D− MEFs, expression of p16, treatment with Cdk4/6 inhibitor) in three different cell types (MEFs, HFFs, U2OS) confirmed that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 was the Rb mono-phosphorylating kinase in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Rb remains hyper-phosphorylated in M phase and is dephosphorylated by activation of the PP1 phosphatase as cells exit mitosis into the next early G1 phase.
source: Rb remains hyper-phosphorylated in M phase and is dephosphorylated by activation of the PP1 phosphatase as cells exit mitosis into the next early G1 phase (Ludlow et al., 1993).
evidence: The manuscript cites a reference supporting this statement.

claim: After nocodazole washout and release of U2OS cells into early G1 phase for 4 hr, all of the hyper-phosphorylated Rb was converted to mono-phosphorylated Rb.
source: After nocodazole washout and release of U2OS cells into early G1 phase for 4 hr, all of the hyper-phosphorylated Rb was converted to mono-phosphorylated Rb.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from nocodazole arrest and release experiments.

claim: Release of U2OS cells from the nocodazole arrest in the presence of the Cdk4/6 inhibitor resulted in the exclusive appearance of un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: However, release of U2OS cells from the nocodazole arrest in the presence of the Cdk4/6 inhibitor (PD0332991) resulted in the exclusive appearance of un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: Nocodazole block and release of HeLa cells in the presence of the Cdk4/6 inhibitor resulted in the presence of only un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Likewise, nocodazole block and release of HeLa cells in the presence of the Cdk4/6 inhibitor (PD0332991) resulted in the presence of only un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: As cells exit mitosis, Rb is fully dephosphorylated to un-phosphorylated Rb, and then rapidly mono-phosphorylated by cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes in early G1 phase.
source: These results determined that as cells exit mitosis, Rb is fully dephosphorylated to un-phosphorylated Rb, and then rapidly mono-phosphorylated by cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes in early G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from mitotic exit experiments.

claim: Rb becomes inactivated by hyper-phosphorylation at the late G1 Restriction point and remains hyper-phosphorylated throughout late G1 phase, S phase, G2 phase, and M phases.
source: Previous studies from our lab and many others have shown that Rb becomes inactivated by hyper-phosphorylation at the late G1 Restriction point and remains hyper-phosphorylated throughout late G1 phase, S phase, G2 phase, and M phases (DeCaprio et al., 1989; Mittnacht et al., 1994; Ezhevsky et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple references supporting this statement.

claim: Hyper-phosphorylated Rb first appears concomitant with activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes.
source: Hyper-phosphorylated Rb first appears concomitant with activation of cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental observations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Selective inhibition of Cdk2 by 15 μM roscovitine resulted in no Cdk2 activity, continued Cdk4/6 activity and the presence of mono-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Selective inhibition of Cdk2 by 15 μM roscovitine, a Cdk2 ATP competitive inhibitor, resulted in no Cdk2 activity, continued Cdk4/6 activity and the presence of mono-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 3I,J).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 3I,J.

claim: Titration of roscovitine from 2 μM to 15 μM resulted in a dose-dependent appearance of intermediate phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
source: Titration of roscovitine from 2 μM to 15 μM resulted in a dose-dependent appearance of intermediate phosphorylated Rb isoforms (Figure 3J), suggesting that unlike cyclin D:Cdk4/6, cyclin E:Cdk2 is a processive Rb kinase.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Unlike cyclin D:Cdk4/6, cyclin E:Cdk2 is a processive Rb kinase.
source: Titration of roscovitine from 2 μM to 15 μM resulted in a dose-dependent appearance of intermediate phosphorylated Rb isoforms (Figure 3J), suggesting that unlike cyclin D:Cdk4/6, cyclin E:Cdk2 is a processive Rb kinase.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the dose-dependent appearance of intermediate forms.

claim: Cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes are the initial Rb hyper-phosphorylating kinase at the late G1 Restriction Point.
source: These observations are entirely consistent with our previous reports that cyclin E:Cdk2 complexes are the initial Rb hyper-phosphorylating kinase at the late G1 Restriction Point (Ezhevsky et al., 1997, 2001; Haberichter et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies by the authors supporting this conclusion.

claim: Treatment of cycling MEFs with a sub-lethal dose (100 ng/ml) of doxorubicin resulted in a G1 phase cell cycle arrest with constitutive cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activity, mono-phosphorylated Rb, and loss of cyclin E/A:Cdk2 activity.
source: Treatment of cycling MEFs with a sub-lethal dose (100 ng/ml) of doxorubicin, a DNA damage-inducing topoisomerase II inhibitor, resulted in a G1 phase cell cycle arrest with constitutive cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activity, mono-phosphorylated Rb, and loss of cyclin E/A:Cdk2 activity (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Doxorubicin treatment of serum-deprived G0 arrested MEFs that contained un-phosphorylated Rb and no cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activity resulted in induction of cyclin D1 and Cdk6, activation of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes and Rb mono-phosphorylation.
source: Surprisingly, doxorubicin treatment of serum-deprived G0 arrested MEFs that contained un-phosphorylated Rb and no cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activity, resulted in induction of cyclin D1 and Cdk6, activation of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes and Rb mono-phosphorylation (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Inhibition of Cdk4/6 activity by retroviral p16 expression in doxorubicin-treated MEFs resulted in the exclusive presence of un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Although several studies have suggested that Rb is phosphorylated during a DNA damage response by non-Cdk kinases, including Chk1/2 and Aurora B (Inoue et al., 2007; Nair et al., 2009), inhibition of Cdk4/6 activity by retroviral p16 expression in doxorubicin-treated MEFs resulted in the exclusive presence of un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 4B,D), thereby excluding the involvement of other kinases.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 4B,D and cites previous studies.

claim: In response to DNA damage, cells select for mono-phosphorylated Rb by activating cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes.
source: Together, these observations demonstrated that in response to DNA damage, cells select for mono-phosphorylated Rb by activating cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from DNA damage experiments.

claim: Treatment of Rb-deleted MEFs expressing ectopic WT Rb-HA with doxorubicin resulted in the presence of mono-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Treatment of Rb-deleted MEFs expressing ectopic WT Rb-HA with doxorubicin resulted in the presence of mono-phosphorylated Rb, whereas Rb-deleted MEFs expressing ectopic ΔCdk Rb-HA contained un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Rb-deleted MEFs expressing ectopic ΔCdk Rb-HA contained un-phosphorylated Rb after doxorubicin treatment.
source: Treatment of Rb-deleted MEFs expressing ectopic WT Rb-HA with doxorubicin resulted in the presence of mono-phosphorylated Rb, whereas Rb-deleted MEFs expressing ectopic ΔCdk Rb-HA contained un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Rb-deleted MEFs showed a >1.6x increase in expression of 173 genes, primarily involved in DNA replication (24%), cell cycle control (20%), and regulation of transcription (18%).
source: Rb is a transcriptional repressor and Rb-deleted MEFs showed a >1.6x increase in expression of 173 genes, primarily involved in DNA replication (24%), cell cycle control (20%), and regulation of transcription (18%) (Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes microarray results summarized in Table 1.

claim: Expression of physiologic levels of mono-phosphorylated WT Rb-HA in Rb-deleted cells restored repression of many genes, especially E2F target genes.
source: Expression of physiologic levels of mono-phosphorylated WT Rb-HA in Rb-deleted cells restored repression of many of these genes, especially E2F target genes (Figure 5C,D; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes microarray results shown in Figure 5C,D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of un-phosphorylated ΔCdk Rb-HA at physiologic levels failed to repress genes and gave a pattern of global transcriptional deregulation similar to Rb-deleted MEFs.
source: However, expression of un-phosphorylated ΔCdk Rb-HA at physiologic levels failed to repress genes and gave a pattern of global transcriptional deregulation similar to Rb-deleted MEFs, suggesting that un-phosphorylated Rb was functionally inactive during a DNA damage response checkpoint during early G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript describes microarray results and infers functional inactivity.

claim: Un-phosphorylated Rb was functionally inactive during a DNA damage response checkpoint during early G1 phase.
source: However, expression of un-phosphorylated ΔCdk Rb-HA at physiologic levels failed to repress genes and gave a pattern of global transcriptional deregulation similar to Rb-deleted MEFs, suggesting that un-phosphorylated Rb was functionally inactive during a DNA damage response checkpoint during early G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the transcriptional deregulation pattern.

claim: WT Rb-HA repressed DHFR and cdc6 E2F target genes, whereas Rb-deleted and un-phosphorylated ΔCdk Rb-HA MEFs showed similar levels of deregulation.
source: Further qRT-PCR analysis of two strong E2F target genes, DHFR and cdc6, showed similar levels of deregulation in both Rb-deleted and un-phosphorylated ΔCdk Rb-HA MEFs, whereas WT Rb-HA repressed both of these genes (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: The manuscript describes qRT-PCR results shown in Figure 5E–G.

claim: Rb-deleted (Rb−/−) MEFs failed to prevent the appearance of tetraploid cells several days after treatment with either doxorubicin or ionizing radiation (20 Grays).
source: Rb-deleted (Rb−/−) MEFs also failed to prevent the appearance of tetraploid cells several days after treatment with either doxorubicin or ionizing radiation (20 Grays) (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 5H,I.

claim: Un-phosphorylated ΔCdk Rb-HA MEFs showed similar high levels of tetraploid cells in response to DNA damage as Rb-deleted (Rb−/−) MEFs.
source: Consistent with the inability to regulate transcriptional control, un-phosphorylated ΔCdk Rb-HA MEFs showed similar high levels of tetraploid cells in response to DNA damage as Rb-deleted (Rb−/−) MEFs.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from tetraploidy analysis.

claim: WT Rb-HA expression rescued the tetraploid phenotype to levels near parental MEFs expressing endogenous wild type Rb.
source: In contrast, WT Rb-HA expression rescued the tetraploid phenotype to levels near parental MEFs expressing endogenous wild type Rb (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 5H,I.

claim: Cells undergoing a DNA damage response activate cyclin D:Cdk4/6 to generate biologically active, mono-phosphorylated Rb, whereas un-phosphorylated was functionally inactive for regulating E2F transcription and preventing the appearance of tetraploid cells.
source: These observations demonstrated that cells undergoing a DNA damage response activate cyclin D:Cdk4/6 to generate biologically active, mono-phosphorylated Rb, whereas un-phosphorylated was functionally inactive for regulating E2F transcription and preventing the appearance of tetraploid cells.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from DNA damage response experiments.

claim: Serum-deprived G0 arrested HFFs and U2OS cells contained un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: The above results demonstrated that un-phosphorylated Rb was non-functional during a DNA damage response. However, serum-deprived G0 arrested HFFs and U2OS cells contained un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 1E,G; Figure 3D), as do quiescent G0 peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBLs) (Ezhevsky et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental observations and cites a previous study.

claim: Quiescent G0 peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBLs) contain un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: The above results demonstrated that un-phosphorylated Rb was non-functional during a DNA damage response. However, serum-deprived G0 arrested HFFs and U2OS cells contained un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 1E,G; Figure 3D), as do quiescent G0 peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBLs) (Ezhevsky et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study supporting this statement.

claim: Rb plays a role in cell cycle exit and differentiation, including proper myogenic development as myoblasts exit the cell cycle into G0.
source: Moreover, other studies have documented a role for Rb in cell cycle exit and differentiation, including proper myogenic development as myoblasts exit the cell cycle into G0 (Gu et al., 1993; Zacksenhaus et al., 1996; Chen and Wang, 2000; Sage et al., 2003; Blais et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple references supporting this statement.

claim: Asynchronous cycling C2C12 myoblasts grown in high mitogen media (FBS) contained both mono-phosphorylated Rb and hyper-phosphorylated Rb with no detectable un-phosphorylated Rb.
source: Asynchronous cycling C2C12 myoblasts grown in high mitogen media (FBS) contained both mono-phosphorylated Rb and hyper-phosphorylated Rb with no detectable un-phosphorylated Rb (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Addition of low mitogen, differentiation media to C2C12 myoblasts induced expression of myotube specific myogenin and resulted in the exclusive presence of un-phosphorylated Rb at day 2.
source: However, addition of low mitogen, differentiation media induced expression of myotube specific myogenin and resulted in the exclusive presence of un-phosphorylated Rb at day 2, concomitant with loss of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 kinase activity and expression of p18, a Cdk4/6-specific inhibitor (Halevy et al., 1995; Franklin and Xiong, 1996; Wang and Walsh, 1996; Zhang et al., 1999) (Figure 6B–D).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 6B–D and cites references.

claim: The exclusive appearance of un-phosphorylated Rb was observed when human HL60 promyelocytic cells were induced to undergo differentiation by addition of retinoic acid.
source: We also observed the exclusive appearance of un-phosphorylated Rb when human HL60 promyelocytic cells were induced to undergo differentiation by addition of retinoic acid (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Reduction of Rb levels by shRNAi resulted in an increased proliferation index (number of nuclei), and increased expression of Mcm3 and Mcm5 (markers of DNA replication).
source: Reduction of Rb levels by shRNAi resulted in an increased proliferation index (number of nuclei), and increased expression of Mcm3 and Mcm5 (markers of DNA replication) (Figure 6F–H, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 6F–H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Physiologic expression of WT Rb-HA compensated for the reduction in endogenous Rb by bringing the proliferation index back to the shScrambled RNAi control.
source: However, physiologic expression of WT Rb-HA compensated for the reduction in endogenous Rb by bringing the proliferation index back to the shScrambled RNAi control.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results from proliferation analysis.

claim: Physiologic expression of ΔCdk Rb-HA resulted in a dramatic reduction of proliferation as cells prematurely exited the cell cycle and decreased Mcm3 and Mcm5 levels.
source: Strikingly, physiologic expression of ΔCdk Rb-HA resulted in a dramatic reduction of proliferation as cells prematurely exited the cell cycle and decreased Mcm3 and Mcm5 levels (Figure 6F–H; Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental results shown in Figure 6F–H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Un-phosphorylated Rb was functionally active to drive cell cycle exit and differentiation of myoblasts into myotubes.
source: Thus, in contrast to the DNA damage response where un-phosphorylated Rb was non-functional, these observations demonstrated that un-phosphorylated Rb was functionally active to drive cell cycle exit and differentiation of myoblasts into myotubes.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from differentiation experiments.

claim: The key tenet of the prevailing model of G1 cell cycle progression proposed that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes inactivated Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylation, termed hypo-phosphorylation.
source: For the last 20 years, the key tenet of the prevailing model of G1 cell cycle progression proposed that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes inactivated Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylation, termed hypo-phosphorylation, resulting in the gradual release of E2F transcription factors that drive cells into late G1 phase.
evidence: The manuscript describes the prevailing model in the field.

claim: Tumor cells expressing wild-type Rb have genetic and epigenetic alterations of the p16 tumor suppressor gene or oncogenic expression of cyclin D1, D2, D3, Cdk4, and Cdk6 genes.
source: This notion was reinforced when tumor cells expressing wild-type Rb were found to have genetic and epigenetic alterations of the p16 tumor suppressor gene or oncogenic expression of cyclin D1, D2, D3, Cdk4, and Cdk6 genes, which became known as the 'p16-cyclin D-Rb' pathway (Sherr, 1994; Sherr and McCormick, 2002; Burkhart and Sage, 2008; Paternot et al., 2010; Henley and Dick, 2012; Choi and Anders, 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple references supporting this statement about cancer genetics.

claim: The large number of tryptic phospho-peptides of 'hypo-phosphorylated' Rb from early G1 cells reported by Mittnacht et al. (1994) was unknowingly misinterpreted and further reinforced the notion that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes inactivate Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylating, hypo-phosphorylation.
source: Moreover, the large number of tryptic phospho-peptides of 'hypo-phosphorylated' Rb from early G1 cells reported by Mittnacht et al. (1994) was unknowingly misinterpreted and further reinforced the notion that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 complexes inactivate Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylating, hypo-phosphorylation.
evidence: The manuscript reinterprets a previous study in light of their new findings.

claim: The notion that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 inactivated Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylating, hypo-phosphorylation was solidified in the 1990s as the model of G1 cell cycle progression.
source: Although there was a complete absence of rigorous biochemical evidence as to the extent of phosphate numbers or kinetics on what was loosely termed hypo-phosphorylated Rb, the notion that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 inactivated Rb by progressive multi-phosphorylating, hypo-phosphorylation was solidified in the 1990s as the model of G1 cell cycle progression.
evidence: The manuscript describes the historical development of the prevailing model.

claim: The Rb gene is transcribed and spliced into a single 4.7 kb mRNA composed of 27 coding exons that does not undergo appreciable alternative splicing and encodes a single 105 kDa protein.
source: The Rb gene is transcribed and spliced into a single 4.7 kb mRNA composed of 27 coding exons that does not undergo appreciable alternative splicing and encodes a single 105 kDa protein (Burkhart and Sage, 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites a reference supporting this statement about Rb gene structure.

claim: Several groups have recently solved the core structure of Rb as an intra-strand pseudo-dimer of dimers with the Cdk sites present on loops between structured regions or on the C-terminus abutting the B-box.
source: Although the complete structure of Rb has yet to be solved, several groups have recently solved the core structure as an intra-strand pseudo-dimer of dimers with the Cdk sites present on loops between structured regions or on the C-terminus abutting the B-box (Burke et al., 2012; Lamber et al., 2013) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript cites structural studies and references Figure 1A.

claim: The generation of 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms may serve as a mechanism to post-translationally functionally diversify Rb in early G1 phase from a single un-phosphorylated isoform in G0.
source: Based on the binding preferences of individual Rb mono-phosphorylated isoforms to specific E2F transcription factors, our data suggest that the generation of 14 mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms may serve as a mechanism to post-translationally functionally diversify Rb in early G1 phase from a single un-phosphorylated isoform in G0.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as an interpretation of their findings.

claim: The substrate recognition of Rb by cyclin D's N-terminal LxCxE motif weak binding to Rb's pocket domain vs cyclins E and A avid binding to four C-terminal R/KxL substrate motifs outside of the pocket likely serves as the defining mechanism between Rb mono-phosphorylation and Rb hyper-phosphorylation.
source: While this will require extensive structural analyses beyond the scope of our study, we speculate that the substrate recognition of Rb by cyclin D's N-terminal LxCxE motif weak binding to Rb's pocket domain (Dowdy et al., 1993) vs cyclins E and A avid binding to four C-terminal R/KxL substrate motifs (Adams et al., 1999) outside of the pocket likely serves as the defining mechanism between Rb mono-phosphorylation and Rb hyper-phosphorylation (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a speculative hypothesis and cites references.

claim: Cyclin E/A:Cdk2's strong binding to the C-terminal tail of Rb would allow access to all 14 Cdk sites on Rb even when transcription factors and chromatin remodeling factors were bound to Rb's pocket and N-terminal binding sites.
source: In this hypothesis, cyclin E/A:Cdk2's strong binding to the C-terminal tail of Rb would allow access to all 14 Cdk sites on Rb even when transcription factors and chromatin remodeling factors were bound to Rb's pocket and N-terminal binding sites.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as part of a speculative hypothesis.

claim: The utilization of the same phosphorylation sites for the activation and inactivation of a protein, albeit with a >12-fold increased phosphate stoichiometry, is an unprecedented mechanism in the literature.
source: We believe that the utilization of the same phosphorylation sites for the activation and inactivation of a protein, albeit with a >12-fold increased phosphate stoichiometry, is an unprecedented mechanism in the literature, but one that also likely applies to Rb-related genes p107 and p130.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as an interpretation of their findings.

claim: The results fundamentally change the understanding of G1 cell cycle regulation to show that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activates Rb for binding cellular targets during early G1 phase by generating 14 independent mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
source: Our study addresses several critical problems arising from numerous biochemical analyses of Rb phosphorylation going back more than 20 years. The results presented here fundamentally change the understanding of G1 cell cycle regulation to show that cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activates Rb for binding cellular targets during early G1 phase by generating 14 independent mono-phosphorylated Rb isoforms.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a major conclusion from the study.

claim: The oncogenic activation of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 results in Rb mono-phosphorylation to drive quiescent G0 cells into a more metabolically active, but early G1 phase arrested phenotype.
source: Given that the majority of human tumors contain wild-type Rb, but select for deregulated cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activity (Sherr and McCormick, 2002; Burkhart and Sage, 2008; Knudsen and Knudsen, 2006; Choi and Anders, 2013), we hypothesize that the oncogenic activation of cyclin D:Cdk4/6 results in Rb mono-phosphorylation to drive quiescent G0 cells into a more metabolically active, but early G1 phase arrested phenotype (Figure 8).
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a hypothesis based on their findings and cites references.

claim: By constitutively mono-phosphorylating Rb, the nascent neoplastic cell avoids cell cycle exit and differentiation mediated by un-phosphorylated Rb, and also maintains a high level of metabolism.
source: By constitutively mono-phosphorylating Rb, the nascent neoplastic cell avoids cell cycle exit and differentiation mediated by un-phosphorylated Rb, and also maintains a high level of metabolism.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as an interpretation of their findings in the context of cancer.

claim: This notion is entirely consistent with the observed subtle and highly tolerated cancer predisposing mutations of p16 deletion and cyclin D overexpression in mouse models that avoid activation of oncogene-induced apoptosis.
source: This notion is entirely consistent with the observed subtle and highly tolerated cancer predisposing mutations of p16 deletion and cyclin D overexpression in mouse models that avoid activation of oncogene-induced apoptosis (Burkhart and Sage, 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites a reference supporting this interpretation.

claim: Cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activity combined with other signal transduction pathway mutations contributes to increased cellular metabolism that is monitored by an unknown metabolic sensor.
source: Cyclin D:Cdk4/6 activity combined with other signal transduction pathway mutations contributes to increased cellular metabolism that we speculate is monitored by an unknown metabolic sensor.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a speculative hypothesis.

claim: Once the metabolic threshold has been exceeded, the sensor activates cyclin E:Cdk2 resulting in Rb inactivation by hyper-phosphorylation, induction of E2F target gene transcription and progression across the Restriction Point into late G1 phase.
source: Once the metabolic threshold has been exceeded, the sensor activates cyclin E:Cdk2 resulting in Rb inactivation by hyper-phosphorylation, induction of E2F target gene transcription and progression across the Restriction Point into late G1 phase (Haberichter et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a speculative hypothesis and cites a reference.
